newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Seven NZ work stoppages ended in May - SNZ.
newsitem.headline: Seven NZ work stoppages ended in May - SNZ.

text.p: Seven work stoppages ended in May 1996, Statistics New Zealand said on Thursday.
Five were complete strikes and two were partial strikes. Together they involved 2,540 employees and resulted in the loss of 4,240 person-days of work and about NZ$658,000 in wages and salaries.

There were 70 stoppages which ended in the 12 months to May, resulting in the loss of 20,587 person-days of work, down from the 51,046 days lost in the year to May 1995 and the 37,643 lost in the year to May 1994.
There were 13,884 employees involved in the stoppages that ended in the year to May 1996, down on 30,308 in the previous year.
An estimated $2.7 million in wages and salaries were lost, down from $6.5 million in the year to May 1995.
Of the 70 stoppages in the year to May, 58 were complete strikes, 11 were partial strikes and one was a complete lockout.
As well as the seven stoppages ended in May, 11 others were still in progress.
